adamw.description: Default. Decoupled weight decay, real autograd, moderate steps.

adamw_decay_only.description: Weight decay as the only driving force (zero-initial gradient is impossible to force, so this preset uses a far-from-optimum start and isolates the decoupled decay term in the update breakdown).

adam.description: L2 weight decay coupled into the gradient by the optimizer itself.

sgd.description: Plain SGD, no momentum, no weight decay: the simplest real update.

sgd_momentum.description: SGD with momentum and Nesterov acceleration.

small_gradient.description: Small-gradient regime: |x| is tiny, so dL/dw is tiny as well.

large_gradient.description: Large-gradient regime: |x| and the initial distance are both large.

near_stationary.description: Near-stationary regime: the parameter starts at the optimum, so the gradient is ~0 from the first step onward.

oscillatory.description: Oscillatory regime: a large learning rate on a sign-alternating input stream is observed for update-sign changes (the sign flip alone does not force the MSE gradient to alternate).

fp32_resolution.description: FP32-resolution-sensitive regime: the learning rate is small enough that the optimizer's candidate update falls below one ULP of the stored float32 value, so updates are attempted but the stored parameter does not move. The start is offset from the known optimum so the gradient is genuinely non-zero - starting exactly at it would make the candidate update zero and demonstrate nothing.

diverging.description: Divergence regime: the learning rate is far outside the stable range, which drives the real loss and the real parameter to non-finite values so the non-finite detector is exercised. Uses the linear (non-tanh) model, because a saturated tanh kills the gradient and the run would stall at a large finite value instead of diverging.
